findings.desc: Lattice-lifecycle-memory-Evolving.md:167-168 - `advisory_memory` and `host_transcript_memory` are defined as scoreable expected layers, but lines 84-89 exclude dev-memory and host/manual transcripts from corpus and gold truth. This makes the MemoryScore contract self-contradictory and could lead a future benchmark to score retrieval over non-authoritative sources. Severity: medium.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in commit 7dbfbf10: advisory_memory and host_transcript_memory are now explicitly boundary-only labels and cannot enter corpus truth, gold truth, HistoricalRetrievalScore, recall, or precision.

findings.desc: Lattice-lifecycle-memory-Evolving.md:135 CHK-001 promises a visible 100-point MemoryScore formula, but the doc only defines QualityScore and then uses `MemoryScore = QualityScore + 10 * ScaleStabilityScore`, forcing readers to expand the weights themselves. Fix by adding the fully expanded MemoryScore equation inline next to the helper notation so the user-visible formula is explicit.

Lattice-lifecycle-memory-Evolving.md:127 adds `current-state query has stale truth hit => FAIL`, but the Failure taxonomy at Lattice-lifecycle-memory-Evolving.md:204 does not name any stale-truth or freshness failure type. Fix by adding a matching taxonomy row or explicitly mapping this hard-fail path to an existing failure class so the contract stays internally consistent.
